title: intent search passes the query into FTS5 unescaped, so any hyphenated term fails with a leaked sqlite error
body:
`intent search` passes the query into FTS5 unescaped, so any hyphenated term fails and the refusal leaks the storage layer.

DRIVEN, 2026-08-31, against a854d7c3:

  $ intent search 'Rate-limited'
  error: the search query `Rate-limited` was refused
    caused by: sqlite: no such column: limited
    caused by: no such column: limited

The hyphen reaches FTS5's query grammar, which reads `Rate-limited` as a column
reference. Two defects in one line.

FIRST, A LARGE AND ORDINARY CLASS OF QUERIES CANNOT BE RUN. Hyphenated terms are
not exotic in this corpus -- `dry-run`, `new-surface`, `read-only`, `to-disk`,
`fail-forward`, `steel-thread` -- so the verb refuses a substantial share of what
an operator would naturally type, and refuses it with an error that gives no clue
that the hyphen is the cause.

SECOND, THE REFUSAL LEAKS THE STORAGE LAYER TO THE OPERATOR. `sqlite: no such
column: limited` names a technology the surface does not otherwise expose and
describes a condition the caller cannot act on. The remedy line is absent
entirely, against the estate's own convention that a refusal names what to do.

The fix is to escape or quote the query before it reaches FTS5, and to refuse
unparseable input in Intent's own voice rather than passing SQLite's through.

Found by dc while driving `docs/getting-started.md` for AC-02.1, where it was
named inside issue 0193 so the page would not be corrected twice. Filed
separately because the page defect and the verb defect want different fixes, and
a verb defect addressed only inside a docs issue is addressed to nobody.
